tips.headline: Check your AI judge against human labels
tips.what: A judge is a model that grades outputs. It can usually be the same model as your main task.
tips.how: Label a held‑out test set by hand. Measure how often the judge agrees on passes and fails.
tips.why: Agreement with people matters most. Try a different judge model only if agreement stays low.

tips.headline: Run agent code in one sandbox on every OS
tips.what: MXC is an open‑source Microsoft library. It runs untrusted code, such as model output, in a sandbox.
tips.how: Install the Rust, .NET or Node SDK. Set allowed paths and network rules in a JSON policy.
tips.why: One setup works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Each system uses its own built‑in sandbox.

tips.headline: Grade each agent run with several typed questions
tips.what: Jev, a fast decision model from TypeSafe, can judge agent runs in LangSmith, a tracing tool.
tips.how: Open the Evaluators tab in a LangSmith tracing project. Ask difficulty and correctness as separate questions.
tips.why: Each question gets its own typed answer in one pass. This tells you more than one pass/fail score.

tips.headline: Fine‑tune on longer text with less GPU memory
tips.what: TRL is a Hugging Face library to fine‑tune models. Version 1.15 adds a memory‑saving step by default.
tips.how: Run `pip install -U trl`. Rerun your DPO or GRPO job with longer examples on a Linux GPU.
tips.why: At 8,192 tokens, peak GPU memory drops 52% to 82%. DPO fits 59,392 tokens, not 10,240.

tips.headline: Build trust in agent output before you scale up
tips.what: Trusted agents let one person ship far more work. Volume only scales after you trust the output.
tips.how: List your ongoing work streams. Give each stream an agent and checks that you trust.
tips.why: Without checks that you trust, you cannot review more work. Trust lets your output grow.

ai.title: Step 5 Preview opens on OpenRouter
ai.body: A mixture‑of‑experts model (27B active, 600B total parameters) with a 1M‑token context. It reads text, images and video. It costs $1.00 per million input tokens.

ai.title: Open training tasks for terminal agents
ai.body: 1,000 tested RL (reinforcement learning) environments and 36,000 agent runs, failures included. Training gemma‑4‑31B‑it on them added 3.1 points on Terminal‑Bench 2.1.

ai.title: Mellum2.1 is a fast open model for coding agents
ai.body: More RL training for agent coding work. The weights are on Hugging Face. GGUF builds for llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio are coming soon.

tool.title: Ultrafast mode for GPT‑6.1 Sol
tool.body: In the API, set `service_tier` to `ultrafast`. It costs $12 per million input tokens and $60 per million output tokens.

tool.title: Video 1.5 Lite is in the API
tool.body: Make video clips from text or an image. It costs $0.02 per second at 480p and $0.03 per second at 720p.

tool.title: Ask follow‑up questions about a chart
tool.body: After `/visualize` draws a chart, ask the next question in the same chat. Cursor answers with a new chart.

jev.title: Step‑Jev scores each agent step
jev.body: Step‑Jev is a Jev judge that grades each step of an agent run. A TypeSafe account says its training reward is stuck.

jev.title: TypeSafe posts a Jev test on email labels
jev.body: TypeSafe posted a test of Jev on email labels. Stay calibrated when you pick a judge.
